note: Vol. I No. 32. THE FULL WITNESS FOR THE JULY 1 LETTER LIST IS IN THIS ISSUE, and it is on PAGE 1 — the segmenter put the list in page 1 column 2 and cut it far less than the issue of 1834-07-02 did, so the sub-column that survives there as bare surnames survives here with its forenames. Every name the previous issue could not mint is minted here. Pages 1 columns 3-6 and 2 are national reprint; the town is in page 3 and page 4, and page 3 columns 3, 5 and 6 are the Tesseract fallback and are the cleanest text in the issue.

claims.notes: RULING 1 — a listed name mints a resident candidate, and `letter_list_only` is true so the compiler keeps the weaker evidence distinguishable. Part 1 of 12 of the list of letters remaining in the Post Office at Chicago on 1 July 1834. THE HEADING is the list's own at lines 369-371: 'List of Letters' / '[REMAIN]ING in the Post-Office at Chicago, Ill. July 1, 1834.', and JOHN S. C. HOGAN, P.M. signs it at line 776. THIS IS THE SAME LIST as the issue of 1834-07-02 carries at page 3 column 2, and it is the BETTER WITNESS: there the two printed sub-columns were cut so that one kept its forenames and lost its surnames and the other lost its forenames, and 128 lines could yield no name at all. Here both sub-columns survive whole enough to name, so the claims in this file supersede nothing — both stand, with their own locators, and a reader comparing them can see which reading each name rests on. THREE STREAMS are woven through this column: the list's two sub-columns and slivers of page 1's body text ('Chid', 'Ite', 'And', 'The'), which are excluded. NORMALIZATION. The left sub-column's FIRST LETTER is what the segmenter damaged — 'onathan Burbee', 'Javid Bigelow', 'larvey A. Blakesley', 'Lobert Baines' — and the restored letter is bracketed in every case ('[J]onathan', '[D]avid', '[H]arvey', '[R]obert'). The restoration is supported by the surname's place in an unbroken alphabetical run and by the forename being a common one; where it is not, the letter stays '[?]' rather than being chosen ('[?]bey Blankinship', '[?]oon Bowrassa', '[?]kiler Brown'). A trailing numeral on a printed line is the count of letters held for that person, not part of the name, and is dropped from `normalized` while staying in the verbatim quote. Nothing is corrected on shape alone. A HAND COUNT, made against this column on 2026-08-28: page 1 column 2 runs 404 lines from 372 to 775; 298 of them are entries in the list and 106 are one- and two-word slivers of the body column woven through it. The extraction holds 298 entries. The issue of 1834-07-16 prints the same list in 373 lines and also yields 298 — two independent segmentations of one printing agreeing on the count, which is the strongest check available without the page images. FOUR NAMES WERE ADDED after the count: 'stephen May', 'handler Fi her', 'JON. awartwout jr.' and 'acob Gur 2', all dropped by a first pass that required a surname of four letters.

claims.notes: THE HARBOUR IS UNDER CONSTRUCTION AND THIS IS THE ADVERTISEMENT FOR ITS STONE — one thousand cords of it, to be delivered INTO THE PIERS, at up to twenty-four cords a day from 10 August 1834, by an officer of the United States Army acting as Superintendent of Public Works. For a reconstruction dated 1835 this is the most consequential infrastructure claim in the July run: it dates the piers, it says they were still being filled a year before the scene, it names the material as prairie stone from near Chicago, and it gives a rate. THE OFFICER'S FORENAME IS NOT PRINTED — 'ALLEN, Lt. U.S. A.' — so the entity is bracketed rather than identified. THE OTHER HALF of this advertisement is in page 3 column 2 at lines 3037-3051, which print 'Stone for', 'the Chicato Harbou', 'works', 'One Thousan', 'The Stone to be', 'each variety, as to', 'orbiding s', 'tendent, by his givin', 'costractors of such', 'Chicago, July 3, 16' — every supply bracketed above was checked against those fragments line by line, and 'the Chicato Harbou[r]' is where the word HARBOUR comes from. THE DATE the other half carries, 'Chicago, July 3, 18[34]', is not quoted here because it is not in this column; it is six days before this issue.
